close_reason: Made SetErrorType::custom canonicalise known wire-names to their typed variants — custom('forbidden') now returns Forbidden, not Custom('forbidden'). Round-trip is symmetric: serde_json::from_str of any known wire-name produces the same typed variant that custom() produces. Implementation: extracted SetErrorType::from_wire_str(&str) -> Option<Self> as the single source of truth; both custom() and the Deserialize visitor use it. Added canonicalise test that spot-checks 6 known wire-names and one unknown ('mdnAlreadySent' stays Custom). Existing custom_round_trips test still passes because 'mdnAlreadySent' is not a known name. Production call sites (sieve.rs invalidSieve/sieveIsActive, mdn.rs mdnAlreadySent, chat message.rs rateLimited, contacts addressbook.rs addressBookHasContents) all use names outside the typed-variant set, so behaviour is unchanged for them.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:276-321 (Serialize + Deserialize for SetErrorType). The Display impl at backend.rs:244-274 emits Custom(s) as the bare string `s`. The Deserialize visitor's match-arm list at backend.rs:292-315 prefers every named variant before falling through to `other => SetErrorType::Custom(other.to_owned())`.

Consequence: SetErrorType::custom("forbidden") and SetErrorType::Forbidden are PartialEq-distinct (the derived PartialEq on the enum sees different variants) but produce the same wire bytes ("forbidden"). Round-trip is asymmetric:

  let x = SetErrorType::custom("forbidden");
  let s = serde_json::to_string(&x)?;          // "\"forbidden\""
  let y: SetErrorType = serde_json::from_str(&s)?;
  assert_eq!(x, y);                            // FAILS: y is Forbidden, not Custom

Real-world failure mode: a handler emits `SetError::new(SetErrorType::custom("forbidden"))` (typo: should have used the named variant). A test deserialises the wire response and compares to `SetErrorType::custom("forbidden")`. The assertion fails with a confusing message — both sides print as "forbidden" via Display, but one is Custom and the other is Forbidden. The reader has to either Debug-print or check the variant tag with discriminant().

Same pattern for every named variant: custom("invalidRecipients") != InvalidRecipients, custom("mailboxHasChild") != MailboxHasChild, etc. 13 mail variants + 10 base variants = 23 names whose Custom-form does not equal their named-form after round-trip.

Right shape (two options):
1. Custom validation: `SetErrorType::custom(s: impl Into<String>) -> Self` returns Custom(s) ONLY if s is not a known wire-name; if it IS a known name, return the corresponding named variant. The Deserialize visitor does the same logic — same code path, single source of truth.

2. PartialEq override: implement PartialEq manually to compare wire strings rather than variant tags. SetErrorType::Forbidden == SetErrorType::Custom("forbidden") becomes true. Hash impl needs the same treatment for HashMap/HashSet consistency.

(1) is cleaner — preserves the typed-pattern-match advantage and eliminates the asymmetry entirely.

A test asserting Custom("forbidden") survives round-trip as Custom would also catch this, but adding the test without (1) or (2) just documents the bug instead of fixing it.
title: SetErrorType::Custom(s) and named variant for same wire string are PartialEq-distinct but serde-asymmetric — silent contract drift on round-trip
